title: School nature club day trail
storyboard: Film: school nature club kids with hand lenses on a Bengaluru trail, naturalist at a weaver-ant nest (2 takes)

scenes.headline: Trail stop 1: a tent made of leaves… by ants
The glue? Silk from their own larvae
scenes.body: Workers pull leaf edges together and use larval silk to bind them.

scenes.headline: Honey bee on a flower
scenes.body: Spot the pollen baskets on its hind legs.

scenes.headline: Monitor lizard on the move
scenes.body: We look, we don't touch. Keoladeo National Park, Rajasthan.

scenes.headline: Day trails for school nature clubs
scenes.body: Hand lenses, field notebooks and a naturalist.

caption:
A Saturday with our school nature club.

Weaver ant larvae don't spin cocoons for themselves — their silk goes into building the colony's leaf nests.

Source: Gadagkar 2021, Resonance (IISc); Animal Diversity Web. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Vlog of a kids' day trail: small, close-up wildlife (ants, bees, lizards) suits a city trail; kid/naturalist shots storyboarded. Weaver-ant nest photo from Kerala.
